journeys.title: Big Cats of India
journeys.description: From the high Himalaya to the last home of the Asiatic lion—a private journey through the landscapes that have always belonged to India’s big cats.
journeys.intro:
India is one of the few places on Earth with an extraordinary constellation of big cats. The snow leopard belongs to the high silence of Ladakh. The tiger inhabits the ancient forests in Rajasthan as one of its many abodes. The leopard, among several other places, lives in the granite country of Jawai, alongside pastoral communities who have lived with them for generations. And in Gujarat, the Asiatic lion survives in the only place on earth where it still occurs in the wild.

Our ‘Big Cats of India’ Signature Journey brings these four worlds together in one private journey. Over four weeks, the landscape changes dramatically – from snowbound Himalayan valleys to dry forest, granite country and sunlit grasslands. And so does the character of your wildlife experience. This circuit is a carefully constructed passage through four of India’s most compelling big-cat habitats, with the time, comfort and our field expertise to experience each on its own terms.

Ladakh: In the trans-Himalaya, the search for the snow leopard is as much about learning the ruggedly beautiful landscape as finding the cat. High valleys, broken ridgelines and extraordinary light make this the most elemental chapter of this Journey.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Arrival in Delhi
days.copy: Arrive in India’s vibrant capital, where centuries-old heritage meets the energy of a modern metropolis. Settle into your hotel, meet your expedition team, and prepare for an extraordinary journey across some of India’s most remarkable wildlife landscapes.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Fly to Ladakh
days.copy: Take a domestic flight from Delhi to Leh, gateway to the high-altitude wilderness of Ladakh. On arrival, transfer to your hotel and begin acclimatising to the altitude. The remainder of the day is at leisure, allowing you to rest and adjust to your new surroundings.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Acclimatisation in Ladakh
days.copy: A minimum of 48 hours in Leh is strongly recommended before venturing into the mountains in search of snow leopards. Spend another leisurely day acclimatising, with the opportunity for gentle excursions around Leh. Explore its ancient monasteries, vibrant markets and historic streets, discovering the cultural heart of this extraordinary Himalayan capital.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Into Snow Leopard Country
days.copy: After an early breakfast, depart Leh in comfortable vehicles and journey deeper into the mountains towards your remote camp, set within prime snow leopard habitat. On arrival, the camp team will welcome you, brief you on the days ahead and introduce you to your surroundings.

days.label: Days 5-9
days.title: Tracking Snow Leopards
days.copy: Spend five full days exploring the rugged valleys and high ridgelines of Ladakh in search of the elusive snow leopard. Our expert spotters will patiently scan the landscape for movement, tracks and other signs of these remarkable cats. When a snow leopard is located, you will be escorted to a suitable vantage point for observation and photography. Hot breakfast and lunch will be served in the field, allowing you to make the most of every daylight hour. Return to camp as the mountains fall into the evening light.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Return to Delhi & Drive to Ranthambhore
days.copy: Depart camp early and travel back to Leh Airport for your flight to Delhi. On arrival, continue overland to Ranthambhore, where you will check into your lodge and settle in for the next chapter of your journey.

days.label: Days 11-14
days.title: Tigers of Ranthambhore
days.copy: Over four days, explore different zones of Ranthambhore National Park in search of tigers and the diverse wildlife that shares their domain. Few tiger habitats are as evocative as Ranthambhore. Ancient ruins and monumental structures dating back centuries rise from the landscape, remnants of the historic fort complex woven into forests, lakes and open grasslands. The setting offers a remarkable sense of wilderness shaped by both nature and history. Each day includes two safaris, offering ample time to explore the park and follow the lives of its wildlife.

days.label: Day 15
days.title: Journey to Jawai
days.copy: Continue overland to Jawai, a striking landscape of volcanic granite, open pastures and scattered scrub, where leopards have adapted to life alongside the region’s pastoral communities. As you travel west, the landscape changes dramatically – from the forests of Ranthambhore to expansive agricultural country punctuated by enormous granite outcrops. This is a very different India, and one of the most unusual habitats in which to encounter a leopard.

days.label: Days 16-17
days.title: Leopards of Jawai
days.copy: Spend two full days exploring Jawai in search of its celebrated leopards. The region’s open terrain and dramatic granite formations offer exceptional opportunities for both observation and photography. Set out on morning and afternoon safaris, watching for leopards emerging from their rocky dens and moving across the boulder-strewn landscape. Between safaris, return to the lodge for meals and time to relax. As evening descends, the granite hills glow in shades of pink and amber, creating an atmospheric backdrop to one of India’s most distinctive wildlife experiences.

days.label: Day 18
days.title: Journey to Gir
days.copy: Continue to the final destination of the expedition. Depart Jawai and drive to Jodhpur Airport for your flight to Diu. On arrival, continue by road for approximately two hours to Gir, home to the last wild population of the Asiatic lion.

days.label: Days 19-20
days.title: Gir, Last Home of the Asiatic Lion
days.copy: Explore Gir, the last refuge of the Asiatic lion and the only place on Earth where this extraordinary big cat can be seen in the wild. Across teak forests, dry deciduous woodland and open scrub, search for lions moving through their ancestral range, along with the rich diversity of wildlife that inhabits this remarkable ecosystem. As with Ranthambhore and Jawai, each day includes two safaris, allowing you to experience Gir at its most active – through the coolness of the early morning and the softer light of late afternoon.

days.label: Day 21
days.title: Departure
days.copy: Your journey concludes with a flight back to Delhi. From the high valleys of Ladakh to the forests of Ranthambhore, the granite hills of Jawai and the dry woodlands of Gir, you leave with memories of four extraordinary landscapes – and encounters with four of India’s most iconic big-cat realms.

body: India is one of the few places on Earth with an extraordinary constellation of big cats. The snow leopard belongs to the high silence of Ladakh. The tiger inhabits the ancient forests in Rajasthan as one of its many abodes. The leopard, among several other places, lives in the granite country of Jawai, alongside pastoral communities who have lived with them for generations. And in Gujarat, the Asiatic lion survives in the only place on earth where it still occurs in the wild.

Our ‘Big Cats of India’ Signature Journey brings these four worlds together in one private journey. Over four weeks, the landscape changes dramatically – from snowbound Himalayan valleys to dry forest, granite country and sunlit grasslands. And so does the character of your wildlife experience. This circuit is a carefully constructed passage through four of India’s most compelling big-cat habitats, with the time, comfort and our field expertise to experience each on its own terms.

Ladakh: In the trans-Himalaya, the search for the snow leopard is as much about learning the ruggedly beautiful landscape as finding the cat. High valleys, broken ridgelines and extraordinary light make this the most elemental chapter of this Journey.

Ranthambhore: Ancient fort walls, ruined temples, lakes and dry forest form the tangible theatre for one of India’s most compelling and popular tiger landscapes. Here, patience can be rewarded by a tiger emerging from the forest and walking — as if an impossibility on the move — through a landscape shaped by centuries of human history.

Gir: There is quite simply nowhere else to see an Asiatic lion in the wild. Gir, more than being another safari destination, is a pilgrimage into the final stronghold of an ancient species – a landscape of dry forest, open country and remarkable conservation significance.

journeys.title: Central India’s Six-Park Safari
journeys.description: Follow the striped big cat through the wild heart of India—in six forests, discover a hundred ways to experience the tiger.
journeys.intro:
Across the forests of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, the tiger tale acquires a different character. In one reserve, it may emerge from the sal at first light, its presence first aurally confirmed by the alarm calls of chital. In another, it may appear beside or in a waterhole in the fierce afternoon heat. In yet another, it may slip between bamboo and shadow before disappearing as quietly as it arrived. The pleasure of seeing a wild tiger, along with learning how to read the forest around it — the tracks, calls, scents, movements and silences — is one of the many timeless experiences this Journey is crafted to offer.

Six parks also mean six distinct worlds of wilderness. Days here are unhurried, away from the usual urban din, with early mornings in the field, long afternoons of stillness and leisure, and evenings returning to the forest as the light softens. Between sightings are the several smaller encounters that make these landscapes whole: the magnificent gaur, the adorable sloth bear, the surreal wild dog and the ever elusive leopard to name a few. And a vast diversity of birds adding sound and colour in these forests.

This Journey is designed for you to linger long enough where the wilderness is known to prize patience. The overland route allows you to explore each forest with time to understand the subtle differences in terrain, vegetation and wildlife behaviour. Comfortable lodges, private vehicles and experienced naturalists bring ease to this grand Central India expedition, while our thoughtful pacing leaves space for those unscripted moments that the wild always offers if one keeps the inner eye and ear open, too.

Seamless overland transfers remove the need for internal flights, allowing India’s changing landscapes to unfold naturally, while thoughtfully selected luxury lodges offer privacy, refinement and an intimate relationship with the wilderness. The itinerary can be extended to cultural icons such as Varanasi, Agra or Jaipur, or onward to Gir for Asiatic lions or the Himalaya for snow leopards, creating a wholly bespoke wildlife-and-culture journey across India.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Arrive in Delhi
days.copy: Arrive in India’s dynamic capital, an ancient city, and settle into your hotel near the airport. Take the evening to relax and recover from your journey, with a restful night before setting out for the forests of Central India.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Delhi to Tadoba
days.copy: Take an early morning flight from Delhi to Nagpur. On arrival, collect your luggage and begin the comfortable three-hour private drive to Tadoba. Check into your lodge and enjoy a leisurely lunch before heading into the forest for your first safari. Return to the lodge for dinner and a relaxed evening.

days.label: Days 3-5
days.title: Safaris in Tadoba
days.copy: Over the next three days, explore Tadoba’s rich forest, meadow and lakes on morning and afternoon safaris. The reserve is home to thriving populations of tigers, leopards, sloth bears and wild dogs, with each outing offering a different perspective on this extraordinary wilderness. Breakfast is carried into the park, allowing you to remain immersed in the forest through the morning before returning to the lodge for lunch and a little time to rest. In the afternoon, head out once again, remaining in the field through the golden hours before returning for dinner.

days.label: Day 6
days.title: Tadoba to Pench
days.copy: Depart early and travel overland to Pench, the forest that has inspired many a popular wild tale. Arrive at your lodge, settle into the surroundings and, after lunch, head out on your first safari through this very different landscape.

days.label: Days 7-8
days.title: Safaris in Pench
days.copy: Spend two full days exploring different areas of Pench and discovering its distinctive forest character. Each day includes two carefully paced safaris, with breakfast enjoyed in the park before returning to the lodge for lunch and a period of relaxation. Later in the afternoon, return to the forest and remain out through sunset, when the changing light and cooling temperatures bring a different rhythm to the wilderness.

days.label: Day 9
days.title: Transfer to Kanha
days.copy: Following an early breakfast, travel overland to Kanha, one of Central India’s most beautiful wilderness landscapes. Vast sal forests and open grasslands are home to barasingha, gaur, leopards and tigers, with the landscape itself becoming an integral part of the experience. Check into your lodge and head out for your first safari.

days.label: Days 10-11
days.title: Safaris in Kanha
days.copy:
Spend two days exploring Kanha’s varied habitats, including its stunning open grasslands throbbing with wildlife. Each day brings two safaris, beginning with an early morning outing and breakfast in the park, followed by a return to the lodge for lunch and time to unwind.

The afternoon safari begins later in the day and continues through sunset, offering the opportunity to experience Kanha as the forest changes character with the fading light.

days.label: Day 12
days.title: Transfer to Bandhavgarh
days.copy: After breakfast, travel onwards to Bandhavgarh, much sought-after for its tigers and ancient fort-topped hills. Arrive at your lodge, settle in and, after lunch, venture into the park for your first safari amid this dramatic landscape.

days.label: Days 13-14
days.title: Safaris in Bandhavgarh
days.copy: Spend two days exploring Bandhavgarh, renowned for its exceptional tiger habitat and the striking terrain surrounding its fabled ancient fort. Safaris take you through forest and open country, where every outing brings the possibility of a memorable encounter against a landscape rich in history and atmosphere.

days.label: Day 15
days.title: Bandhavgarh to Panna
days.copy: Begin with a final morning safari in Bandhavgarh before returning to the lodge for breakfast. Check out and continue overland to Panna, arriving in the late afternoon. Settle into your lodge and enjoy a quiet evening at leisure.

days.label: Days 16-18
days.title: Safaris in Panna Tiger Reserve
days.copy: Enter Panna’s dramatic wilderness, where sandstone gorges, waterfalls and the pristine Ken River shape an extraordinary Tiger landscape. Explore the reserve by jeep and boat, with opportunities to encounter tigers, leopards, crocodiles, raptors and a rich diversity of other wildlife. The character of Panna is markedly different from the forests encountered earlier in the journey: more expansive, sculpted and riverine, with the gorgeous Ken adding another dimension to the safari experience.

days.label: Day 19
days.title: Transfer to Satpura
days.copy: Conclude the journey in Satpura, a quieter and more intimate wilderness of rolling hills, dense forests and river valleys. Depart Panna early and travel south towards Satpura. Arrive at your lodge, settle in and, time permitting, head out for an afternoon safari.

days.label: Days 20-21
days.title: Safaris in Satpura
days.copy: Spend your final two days exploring different parts of Satpura, with two safaris each day and ample time to experience the reserve at an unhurried pace. Enjoy breakfast in the park before returning to the lodge for lunch and a period of rest. Later, venture out again in the afternoon and remain in the forest through sunset, when Satpura’s hills, valleys and woodland take on an especially atmospheric character.

days.label: Day 22
days.title: Departure
days.copy: After breakfast, depart Satpura for Bhopal Airport for your return flight to Delhi, bringing your journey through six of Central India’s great Tiger landscapes to a close.

journeys.title: Deserts, Lions & Dunes
journeys.description: Across western India lie landscapes that feel almost untouched by time , grasslands rippling with antelope, salt deserts shimmering like glass, granite hills concealing.
journeys.intro:
Across western India lie landscapes that feel almost untouched by time , grasslands rippling with antelope, salt deserts shimmering like glass, granite hills concealing secretive leopards, and ancient forests resonant with the calls of lions.

This four-habitat, four-big-cat expedition journeys through India’s wildest frontiers, unfolding from Gir to Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, Jawai, and the Desert National Park.

Designed for travellers drawn to remote wilderness without compromise, the experience blends dramatic terrain, rare predators, and immersive cultural encounters, all supported by seamless logistics and refined comfort. Journey through four strikingly different landscapes in pursuit of India’s most iconic predators and desert-adapted wildlife.

From the lions of Gir and the leopards of Jawai to the distinctive fauna of Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, and the Desert National Park, this fully bespoke, all-inclusive expedition reveals the raw drama of western India’s wilderness. Optional travel aboard business jets ensures seamless transitions and refined comfort across vast and contrasting regions.

body: Journey through four strikingly different landscapes in pursuit of India’s most iconic predators and desert-adapted wildlife. From the lions of Gir and the leopards of Jawai to the distinctive fauna of Velavadar, the Rann of Kutch, and the Desert National Park, this fully bespoke, all-inclusive expedition reveals the raw drama of western India’s wilderness.
Optional travel aboard business jets ensures seamless transitions and refined comfort across vast and contrasting regions.

In the rugged teak and acacia forests of Gir, the world’s last Asiatic Lions continue a lineage that once roamed from India to the Mediterranean. Safaris reveal not just lions, but the rhythm of a thriving ecosystem,Jungle Cats slinking through undergrowth, Hyenas trotting across trails, and flocks of birds gathering along seasonal streams. Quiet evenings in your lodge offer a peaceful counterpoint to the day’s excitement.

Velavadar feels like a living canvas,golden grasslands brushed by the wind and dotted with elegant Blackbucks. Here, wolf packs navigate vast open plains, foxes emerge at twilight, and raptors ride warm thermals above. The simplicity of the landscape creates striking photographic compositions and an atmosphere of profound solitude.

The Rann of Kutch introduces an entirely different mood: an endless salt wilderness where the horizon dissolves into shimmering heat. Safaris bring encounters with the rare Asiatic Wild Ass and other desert-adapted wildlife. Dawn and dusk paint the flats in soft pinks and silvers, transforming the desert into a surreal, dreamlike world.

Arriving in Jawai feels like stepping into a mythic realm of stone. Giant granite boulders rise from pastoral plains, forming natural fortresses where leopards thrive. This is a landscape shaped as much by coexistence as geology,Rabari herders move through the terrain with their livestock while leopards watch silently from the rocks.
The resulting harmony offers exceptional opportunities for close yet ethical leopard sightings.

In the Desert National Park, wind-sculpted dunes and thorny scrub create one of India’s most dramatic and fragile ecosystems. Desert Cats slip between shadows, Wolves traverse ridges, and Hyenas work the night. The vastness here is humbling, offering a rare sense of isolation found in few places on earth. After your final explorations, depart carrying the essence of India’s wild frontiers.

Conclude your adventure in Ranthambhore National Park, one of India’s most iconic tiger reserves. Here, the Royal Bengal Tiger roams amidst ancient temples, lakes, and fort ruins , a perfect blend of history and wilderness. Each moment offers the thrill of discovery in a land where time and nature stand still.

This journey unfolds like a desert wind, shifting in texture, tone, and rhythm as it moves across four of India’s most distinctive wilderness habitats. It begins in the lion-ruled forests of Gir, where dry teak woodland and open scrub sustain the last natural population of Asiatic lions, a landscape shaped as much by conservation success as by ancient ecological balance.
Every rustle in the undergrowth carries a sense of quiet authority.

From here, the scenery opens into the luminous grasslands of Velavadar, one of India’s finest and least-altered savannah ecosystems. Vast horizons, seasonal grasses, and salt flats support elegant blackbuck, coursing predators, and a remarkable density of birdlife, offering a visual clarity rare in the subcontinent.

The journey then enters the stark brilliance of the Rann of Kutch, an immense salt desert that feels almost lunar in scale. Here, life has adapted to extremes,Asiatic wild ass move across the white expanse, migratory birds gather at seasonal wetlands, and the silence itself becomes part of the experience. Jawai follows, adding a powerful sense of harmony between people, stone, and wildlife.
Ancient granite hills shelter leopards that coexist with pastoral communities, temples rising naturally from rock formations shaped over millennia.

The expedition concludes in the sweeping isolation of the Desert National Park, where arid grasslands and sand dunes support some of India’s most specialised desert species. Together, these regions form a rare and revealing portrait of India’s western wildlands,diverse, resilient, and deeply evocative.

journeys.intro:
Explore India’s most iconic travel circuit,the Golden Triangle, enhanced by the quiet thrill of a tiger safari in Ranthambore National Park. This journey weaves architectural grandeur, cultural depth, and evocative wildlife encounters into a seamless introduction to the heritage and diversity of North India.

Experience Delhi’s vibrant interplay of history and modern life as you travel through India’s legendary Golden Triangle. Witness the timeless beauty of the Taj Mahal, enjoy immersive tiger safaris in Ranthambore National Park, and explore Jaipur’s colourful bazaars and regal monuments.

With flexible accommodation options, optional private jet upgrades, and fully customisable routing, this journey is thoughtfully crafted for comfort, cultural depth, and unforgettable wildlife encounters.

body: Arrive in India’s capital and explore the contrasts of Old and New Delhi. Wander through bustling bazaars, historic mosques, or iconic landmarks such as India Gate and Humayun’s Tomb before settling into your hotel.
Travel to Agra to experience the magnificence of the Taj Mahal. Visit the Agra Fort and enjoy the changing hues of the marble masterpiece as the day transitions from afternoon to evening.

Continue to Ranthambhore National Park for two days of wildlife exploration. Embark on guided safaris in search of Bengal Tigers, Sloth Bears, and rich birdlife amid ancient ruins, serene lakes, and the dramatic cliffs surrounding the Ranthambhore Fort.

Journey to Jaipur, the Pink City known for its vibrant markets and regal heritage. Discover the Amber Fort, City Palace, and Hawa Mahal, and enjoy free time to shop for textiles, jewellery, and handicrafts. Relax in a heritage palace or luxury boutique retreat.
After a leisurely morning in Jaipur, transfer to the airport for your onward journey. Optional extensions include Delhi, Udaipur, Varanasi, or other destinations across Rajasthan.

The Golden Triangle with Tigers tour seamlessly weaves together India’s cultural heartland and its most iconic wildlife landscapes. Delhi’s dynamic streets set the rhythm of the nation, Agra’s marble mausoleum reveals a timeless love story carved in stone, and Ranthambore National Park introduces the quiet thrill of tracking tigers through forests once shaped by royal hunts.
The journey culminates in Jaipur, where palaces, hilltop forts, and bustling bazaars bring the experience to a vibrant crescendo.

Together, these moments offer an authentic and immersive portrait of India, its artistry, heritage, and natural beauty crafted to inspire, enrich, and captivate first-time and seasoned travellers alike.

journeys.title: India’s Big Five Safari
journeys.description: India’s most remarkable large mammals brought together across UNESCO-listed floodplains, tiger forest and the last wild home of the Asiatic lion.
journeys.intro:
India nurtures diverse wildernesses that in turn nurture vast worlds of wildlife species. This Journey takes you across contrasting habitats – from the lush floodplains of the Northeast to the ancient forests and dry plains of the West, offering you a glimpse into some of India’s most compelling wildlife in one sweeping expedition.

Explore a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can seek India’s Big Five, and explore the potential to encounter rarities such as the almost mythic golden tiger, returning each evening to handpicked lodges and wilderness retreats, chosen for your privacy and unwinding.

Thoughtfully customisable by our experts, this Journey combines exceptional wildlife encounters with seamless travel, cultural depth and the option of private aviation aboard our company-owned business jets, whenever you desire.

highlights: Travel through four distinct wilderness regions — following the trails of India’s Big Five — through some of India’s most exquisite national parks, including a UNESCO World Heritage Site shaped by centuries of natural evolution. Explore the potential to encounter rarities such as the almost mythic golden tiger, which is an added, exceptional dimension to Kaziranga, while more than 400 bird species bring each landscape vividly to life. Fully curated and all-inclusive, with optional private jet travel and cultural extensions available, this Journey is defined by privileged access, unhurried days and an effortless level of comfort.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Delhi
days.copy: Arrive in India’s dynamic capital, where ancient Mughal grandeur mingles with today’s modern life. Settle into your hotel and ease into the journey ahead, or spend the day exploring Delhi’s manifold heritage, vibrant markets and celebrated culinary scene at your own pace.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Fly to Guwahati · Drive to Kaziranga
days.copy: This morning, take a domestic flight to Guwahati, followed by a private road transfer to Kaziranga. Settle into your lodge and, time permitting, venture out on your first afternoon safari.

days.label: Days 3-4
days.title: Safaris in Kaziranga
days.copy: Enter the verdant wilderness of Assam and explore Kaziranga, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India’s great strongholds for the magnificent one-horned rhino. Dawn- and dusk-safaris unfold across vast floodplains, where elephants, water buffalo and deer move through tall grasslands alive with birdlife. At times, the elephant grass can part and open up something magically rare: the golden tiger, a striking colour morph that has captivated wildlife enthusiasts in recent years. The massivity of the Brahmaputra frames this immense wilderness, lending stunning scale, atmosphere and constantly changing light to the experience.

days.label: Day 5
days.title: Last Safari · Drive to Guwahati · Fly to Jaipur
days.copy: Begin with one final safari in Kaziranga before your private transfer back to Guwahati. Board an evening flight to Jaipur, where you will settle in for a comfortable overnight stay before continuing the journey south-west.

days.label: Day 6
days.title: Transfer to Ranthambhore
days.copy: After a leisurely breakfast, check out and drive to Ranthambhore, a journey of approximately three hours. Arrive at your lodge, settle into your surroundings and enjoy lunch before heading out for your first safari in this remarkable landscape.

days.label: Days 7-10
days.title: Ranthambhore National Park
days.copy: Ranthambhore brings together wilderness, human history and the unmistakable atmosphere of Rajasthan enveloping its wilderness. Safaris take you through dry forest, lakes and open country, with ancient temples and the imposing thousand-year-old fort providing a dramatic backdrop to encounters with royal Bengal tigers. Leopards, sloth bears, jackals and an exceptional diversity of birdlife add depth to the experience. Days here are deliberately unhurried, balancing time in the field with the attentive hospitality, privacy and comfort of your lodge.

days.label: Day 11
days.title: Transfer to Gir
days.copy: Depart Ranthambhore early and drive to Delhi Airport for your flight to Rajkot. On arrival, continue by private road transfer to Gir and check into your lodge, marking the beginning of the final wildlife chapter of the journey.

days.label: Days 12-14
days.title: Safaris in Gir National Park
days.copy: The final chapter is planned in the dry forests of western Gujarat – the only place on Earth where Asiatic lions continue to roam in the wild. Encountering them here is more than a remarkable wildlife experience; it offers an intimate perspective on a species whose story is one of extraordinary survival and conservation. Alongside the lions, Gir is home to leopards, hyenas and diverse herbivores moving through teak and acacia woodland. These final safaris complete a journey through four very different wildernesses, bringing together India’s great cats in a way few journeys can.

days.label: Day 15
days.title: Travel to Mumbai · Departure
days.copy: After breakfast, travel to Mumbai for your onward journey, bringing this extraordinary passage through India’s great wildlife landscapes to a close.

faqs.question: Is this a fixed itinerary?
faqs.answer: No. This is something akin to a blueprint. Dates, pacing, lodge character, transfers and field priorities are refined around you and your preferences before confirmation.

faqs.question: Can the journey be shortened?
faqs.answer: Yes. The full route is designed as an immersive experience, but individual sections can be adapted depending on your priorities.

faqs.question: Can we add India’s cultural landmarks?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Any city/town in and around the regions/states part of this itinerary can be incorporated before, after or between the wildlife chapters.

faqs.question: Are the Big Five wildlife sightings guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. And we would never suggest otherwise. Wildlife is wild. Our job is to put you in the right landscape, at the right time, with the right people – and give the experience enough time to happen to you.

faqs.question: Is this suitable for families?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the journey is private, its pace can be adapted to different ages, interests and energy levels.

journeys.title: India’s Small Cats Safari
journeys.description: Felines have held human imagination since antiquity, woven into myth and memory..
journeys.intro:
Felines have held human imagination since antiquity, woven into myth and memory. While the great cats command reverence, their smaller kin remain shadows, reclusive, secretive, and exquisitely adapted to life unseen. Every encounter with them feels earned, fleeting, and profoundly intimate.

This expedition is conceived as a quiet pursuit of those rarities: India’s elusive small cats, the true phantoms of the wild. Spanning 21 days, the journey traces an elegant arc across India’s most contrasting ecosystems, each selected for its potential to reveal a different small cat species.

From the mangrove-fringed wetlands near Kolkata to the vast grasslands of Velavadar, the sculpted granite hills of Jawai, and the stark desert margins around Jaisalmer, the expedition reveals how climate, terrain, and isolation have shaped these remarkable predators.

Night drives and nocturnal explorations, time-intensive tracking with specialist naturalists, and extended stays in each landscape create rare opportunities for observation and photography, without haste or intrusion. This is a deeply immersive, once-in-a-lifetime passage into India’s most enigmatic carnivores and the extraordinary landscapes they quietly inhabit.

body: Spanning 21 days, the journey traces an elegant arc across India’s most contrasting ecosystems, each selected for its potential to reveal a different small cat species.

This 21-day specialist journey traverses four distinct habitats,urban wetlands, open grasslands, rugged rocky hills, and arid desert ecosystems,offering rare opportunities to photograph India’s most elusive small cats, including the fishing cat, jungle cat, rusty-spotted cat, and desert cat.

Designed as a fully inclusive and seamlessly orchestrated wilderness experience, the expedition combines expert-led exploration with exceptional photographic access, while ensuring effortless travel aboard company-owned business jets. Guests may also choose to extend the journey to India’s iconic tiger reserves, creating one of the most comprehensive and immersive wild-India expeditions available.

Arrive in Kolkata and settle into the rhythm of eastern India’s cultural capital. By night, explore the fringes of the city where wetlands, fishponds, and mangrove edges support thriving populations of the elusive Fishing Cat. Expert trackers lead nocturnal excursions offering rare photographic opportunities. Days allow time to experience Kolkata’s vibrant markets, colonial heritage, and culinary landscape.

Travel west to Velavadar, a vast expanse of golden grasslands home to Jungle Cats, Indian Wolves, Jackals, and Blackbuck herds. Early mornings and late afternoons provide optimal light as Jungle Cats hunt rodents and birds across open plains. With extended time in the ecosystem, you can focus on behavior, tracking, and long-lens photography while enjoying the serene, open landscapes.

Continue to Jawai, where granite boulders, caves, and scrub forest create ideal terrain for the Rusty-spotted Cat , the world’s smallest wild cat. Safaris traverse rocky outcrops also known for thriving Leopard populations and dramatic scenery. Spend unhurried days and nights exploring this unique co-existence landscape, capturing rare species in rugged, atmospheric settings.

Enter the stark beauty of the Thar Desert, where sweeping dunes and sparse scrub support the adaptable Desert Cat. With its superb camouflage, sightings reward patient scanning and quiet observation. Track natural water sources and rodent hotspots, while also photographing desert foxes, eagles, vultures, and other arid-zone specialists. Evenings highlight some of India’s finest desert skies.

Conclude your journey with a transfer to Jaisalmer Airport. Optional extensions include Ranthambhore for Tigers, Gir for Asiatic Lions, or Ladakh for Snow Leopards , allowing you to build the most comprehensive cat-focused expedition in India.

The journey unfolds as a rare passage through India’s most diverse small-cat landscapes, each region offering a distinct setting and signature encounter. The wetlands around Kolkata introduce the fishing cat, a globally vulnerable species and one of the few felines in the world adapted to semi-aquatic life, often encountered along marshes and canals at dusk.

In the open grasslands of Velavadar, jungle cats move with confidence through tall grasses and scrub, drawn by abundant prey and the wide-open visibility of one of India’s finest remaining grassland ecosystems.

Jawai’s ancient granite hills bring a sense of intimacy and rarity, offering one of the best chances to encounter the rusty-spotted cat, the smallest wild cat on Earth, seldom seen despite its presence across parts of India.

The journey concludes in the Thar Desert, where patience is rewarded as the desert cat, among the country’s least-observed felines, emerges briefly against moonlit dunes, shaped by extremes of heat, wind, and scarcity. Together, these landscapes create a seamless narrative of discovery, a richly layered exploration of India’s most elusive wild cats and the extraordinary terrains they inhabit.

journeys.title: Ladakh - Land of high passes
journeys.description: This voyage unfurls like a meditation across a land that feels both primal and deeply contemplative.
journeys.intro:
This voyage unfurls like a meditation across a land that feels both primal and deeply contemplative. In Ladakh, colour arrives sparingly yet with intent. Turquoise lakes set against vast sweeps of ochre rock, whitewashed monasteries clinging improbably to cliffs, and prayer flags fluttering amidst profound stillness.

The landscape asks for presence, revealing itself slowly through shifting light, deep silence, and scale. Within this rarefied milieu, the journey opens a window to some of the Himalaya’s most extraordinary life forms.

The expedition seamlessly weaves cultural discovery with rare wildlife encounters, offering the exceptional opportunity to observe snow leopards and the elusive Pallas’ cat in their remote, high-altitude domain.

From the vibrant bazaars and Tibetan rhythms of Leh to the sweeping silence of the trans-Himalayan plateau, each moment unfolds amid dramatic scenery, resilient alpine fauna, and a quiet spiritual gravity. Seamless travel, thoughtfully chosen stays, and some of the best trackers from the region make the experience truly rewarding.

This tour is a powerful synthesis of serenity, adventure, and elemental beauty.

highlights: Travel deep into Ladakh’s high-altitude wilderness, crossing dramatic mountain passes and entering a world shaped by Tibetan culture, vast plateaus, and elemental silence. Guided by expert trackers and long-standing local partnerships essential for operating in this demanding terrain, the journey offers rare chances to observe snow leopards and the elusive Pallas’ cat, alongside hardy alpine species such as blue sheep and ibex. Thoughtfully paced and seamlessly supported, the experience balances rugged exploration with carefully chosen comforts , from warm, intimate lodges to effortless transfers aboard our business jets. Designed with precision and respect for place, this expedition reflects Safari Crafters’ commitment to exceptional field expertise, trusted collaborations, and a level of care that allows guests to experience Ladakh’s extremes with confidence, depth, and quiet refinement.

Arrive in India’s bustling capital and settle into your hotel. Rest and prepare for your flight into the high Himalayas the following morning.

Fly to Leh with breathtaking aerial views of the snow-bound peaks. Spend two days acclimatizing while exploring Leh’s monasteries, markets, and Tibetan-influenced culture. Gentle walks and guided visits prepare you for higher altitudes ahead.

Enter the vast wilderness of Hemis National Park, home to one of the world’s highest densities of Snow Leopards. With expert trackers, follow the trails of the “Grey Ghost” across ridges and valleys. Each day offers opportunities to photograph mountain wildlife including Himalayan Blue Sheep, Ibex, Red Foxes, and numerous high-altitude birds.
Nights are spent in warm, comfortable lodges or homestays tuned to the extreme climate.

Travel to Pangong Lake (summer only) to witness its shifting turquoise hues set against stark mountains. Continue to Hanle, an isolated plateau renowned for sightings of the rare Pallas’ Cat and high-altitude species such as the Black-necked Crane. The region’s silence, night skies, and sweeping vistas offer unmatched Himalayan solitude.
Return to Leh for your scenic flight back to Delhi, carrying memories of stark deserts, sacred monasteries, and the elusive cats of the high Himalayas.

Ladakh is one of the planet’s most extreme inhabited landscapes, a high-altitude desert where survival is shaped by altitude, weather, and time itself. The journey begins in Leh, where gradual acclimatisation is essential, and where centuries-old Tibetan-Buddhist culture offers insight into how human life has adapted to thin air, long winters, and vast isolation.

From Leh, the expedition moves into the immense expanse of Hemis National Park, the largest protected area in India and one of the most important snow leopard landscapes in the world. This rugged terrain of razor-edged ridges, deep valleys, and scree slopes supports a finely balanced alpine ecosystem, with blue sheep and Ibex forming the prey base that sustains the snow leopard.
Wildlife encounters here are earned through patience, skilled tracking, and an intimate understanding of terrain and movement.

The journey then opens into the vast trans-Himalayan plateaus of Pangong Lake and Hanle, where altitude increases and the landscape broadens into sweeping valleys and high-altitude wetlands. These regions support specialised species such as the Pallas’ cat and migratory cranes, while remote monasteries and nomadic settlements reflect centuries of spiritual resilience.
Together, these landscapes reveal Ladakh in its fullest form, stark, demanding, and profoundly alive, offering a rare understanding of one of the world’s most formidable wilderness regions.

journeys.title: Palaces and Tigers
journeys.description: India in its most royal expression—from palatial Rajasthan to tiger forest, leopard country and the shimmering lakes of Udaipur.
journeys.intro:
This is India at its most royal – a journey through palaces, fortresses, gardens and wilderness formed by centuries of power, artistry, imagination and evolution. In Jaipur, the legacy of Rajasthan’s maharajas endures in splendid palaces, ornate courtyards and monumental architecture. The sheer range of colours, the intricacy of craftsmanship and the scale of ambition have been storytelling just what royal meant to the Rajasthanis. In Agra, that grandeur reaches its finest expression, in an architectural legacy whose beauty has endured across centuries, symbolising powerful human emotions.

Between them lies Ranthambhore, where royalty takes on an absolute wild form. Beneath the ancient walls of a formidable hilltop fort, among banyan trees, lakes and dry forest, the royal Bengal tiger lives in its domain with an authority that feels almost elemental. This is a creature whose presence seems perfectly at home in this landscape of kings. And it spells magnificence, self-assuredness, entirely sovereign.

A tiger appearing in the amber light in Ranthambhore, against the ruins of a medieval fortress or beside a still forest lake, symbolises something unique: the grandeur created by human hands meeting the majesty of an older wild sovereign that has ruled these forests far longer than any dynasty.
highlights: Journey through Rajasthan’s royal heartlands defined by changing landscapes, sensational architecture and human history that remains vividly alive. In this part of India, desert fortresses rise from the sands, palace facades shimmer across still lakes and bazaars bustle with rich colours and craftsmanship. Beyond the old cities, the wild reveals another side of Rajasthan – through early-morning forest-tracks, sun-warmed granite hills, distant alarm calls, and skies and ether alive with birdlife. Quiet moments of observing the natural world can lead to the privilege of witnessing India’s great big cats like tigers and leopards in their natural realm. Evenings are spent in reminiscence, in chosen heritage hotels, wilderness lodges and palace retreats, where your privacy has the backdrop of beauty and character. Optional private jet travel and iconic extensions, including the Taj Mahal, allow the journey to leaf through effortlessly from one extraordinary chapter to the next.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Arrive in Delhi
days.copy: Arrive in India’s capital and settle into your hotel. Explore the city at leisure or simply unwind before your Rajasthan adventure begins.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Transfer to Ranthambhore
days.copy: Travel to Ranthambhore National Park, where ancient temples and fortress walls rise above lakes and forest. A scenic five-hour private drive from Delhi brings you to the lodge around lunchtime, followed by your first safari into this remarkable wilderness.

days.label: Days 3-4
days.title: Ranthambhore
days.copy: Spend two safaris each day exploring Ranthambhore in search of tigers, leopards, sloth bears and abundant birdlife. Return to your lodge between drives for leisurely meals, quiet relaxation and conversations with experienced naturalists about the day’s encounters.

days.label: Day 5
days.title: Last Morning in Ranthambhore and Transfer to Jaipur
days.copy: Enjoy one final morning safari before travelling to Jaipur, the celebrated Pink City, where vibrant bazaars, grand palaces and intricate architecture offer an elegant introduction to Rajasthan’s regal heritage.

days.label: Day 6
days.title: Full Day of Sightseeing in Jaipur
days.copy: Discover Jaipur’s architectural treasures, including Amber Fort, City Palace and Hawa Mahal, or browse its lively bazaars for exquisite textiles, jewellery and traditional crafts. The city’s distinctive blend of artistry, history and colour captures the grandeur of Rajasthan.

days.label: Day 7
days.title: Flight to Jaisalmer
days.copy: Take a flight from Jaipur to Jaisalmer, the golden city rising dramatically from the Thar Desert.

days.label: Day 8
days.title: Full Day of Sightseeing in Jaisalmer
days.copy: Explore Jaisalmer’s magnificent sandstone architecture, from ornate havelis to the imposing desert fort. Wander through its intricately carved interiors and historic quarters before watching the dunes take on a warm golden glow as the sun begins to set.

days.label: Day 9
days.title: Overland Transfer to Jodhpur
days.copy: Enjoy a relaxed morning before travelling to Jodhpur, the Blue City, dominated by the magnificent Mehrangarh Fort. Explore its imposing ramparts and palatial interiors, then wander through the old city’s distinctive blue-hued lanes.

days.label: Day 10
days.title: Morning in Jodhpur, Transfer to Jawai
days.copy: Visit Jaswant Thada and the museum at Umaid Bhawan Palace before departing for Jawai. Arrive among its extraordinary granite hills, where Leopards share this ancient landscape with pastoral communities in one of India’s most remarkable examples of coexistence.

days.label: Days 11-12
days.title: Safaris in Jawai
days.copy: Spend these days exploring Jawai’s granite outcrops and tracking its elusive leopards. Between safaris, retreat to your lodge and enjoy the extraordinary tranquillity of a landscape where wildlife and pastoral life continue to exist side by side.

days.label: Day 13
days.title: Jawai to Udaipur
days.copy: Depart Jawai for Udaipur, pausing at the grand Jain temples of Ranakpur en route. Arrive in the City of Lakes and spend the afternoon at leisure, perhaps over an elegant dinner overlooking the shimmering waters of Lake Pichola.

days.label: Day 14
days.title: Udaipur
days.copy: Cruise across Lake Pichola, explore the magnificent City Palace and relax in your lakeside retreat, framed by the Aravalli hills. Take in the enduring legacy of the Maharanas of Mewar as this journey through Rajasthan’s royal heart draws to a close.

days.label: Day 15
days.title: Departure from Udaipur
days.copy: Depart Udaipur with a deeper appreciation of Rajasthan’s extraordinary cultural legacy, architectural splendour and wild landscapes.

body: This is India at its most royal – a journey through palaces, fortresses, gardens and wilderness formed by centuries of power, artistry, imagination and evolution. In Jaipur, the legacy of Rajasthan’s maharajas endures in splendid palaces, ornate courtyards and monumental architecture. The sheer range of colours, the intricacy of craftsmanship and the scale of ambition have been storytelling just what royal meant to the Rajasthanis. In Agra, that grandeur reaches its finest expression, in an architectural legacy whose beauty has endured across centuries, symbolising powerful human emotions.

Between them lies Ranthambhore, where royalty takes on an absolute wild form. Beneath the ancient walls of a formidable hilltop fort, among banyan trees, lakes and dry forest, the royal Bengal tiger lives in its domain with an authority that feels almost elemental. This is a creature whose presence seems perfectly at home in this landscape of kings. And it spells magnificence, self-assuredness, entirely sovereign.

A tiger appearing in the amber light in Ranthambhore, against the ruins of a medieval fortress or beside a still forest lake, symbolises something unique: the grandeur created by human hands meeting the majesty of an older wild sovereign that has ruled these forests far longer than any dynasty.

The moments of watching a tiger may last only seconds, but the memories will endure, much like the forts and palaces themselves. From Jaipur’s royal courts to Ranthambhore’s wilderness and Agra’s architectural masterpieces, this is a Journey through three extraordinary expressions of grandeur – the royalty of India as imagined and built; and the royalty of the wild, embodied in the tiger.

journeys.title: Pink City with Pink Panthers
journeys.description: Jaipur is a symphony of heritage and lineage, of grandeur and simple tidings.
journeys.intro:
Jaipur is a symphony of heritage and lineage, of grandeur and simple tidings. Palaces rise with quiet confidence, their latticed windows filtering light the way memory filters time, while mighty forts crown distant hills, standing sentinel over centuries of ambition, artistry, and royal command. Yet Jaipur is also untamed.

Just beyond the city’s vibrant pulse lies Jhalana Leopard Reserve, a rare and unexpected wilderness where leopards move silently through rocky ridges and scrub forests, and jungle cats slip between shadows at dusk.

Arrive in India’s capital and settle in before your journey to Rajasthan. Depending on your arrival time, you may explore local markets or relax at your hotel.

Travel to Jaipur and immerse yourself in the Pink City’s regal charm. Visit the Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and vibrant bazaars filled with textiles, jewelry, and handicrafts. Wander historic lanes and capture the city’s architectural elegance and lively atmosphere.

Venture into Jhalana Forest Reserve for morning and evening safaris in search of Leopards, Jungle Cats, and other wildlife. Jaipur stands as one of India’s earliest planned royal cities, shaped by principles of Vedic architecture and astronomy. Its forts, palaces, and harmonious street layouts reflect the vision, power, and artistic legacy of the Rajput rulers. Beyond this historic urban fabric lies Jhalana, once a royal hunting landscape and today a protected forest at the city’s edge.
Here, leopards and other native wildlife move through rocky hills and dry deciduous woodland, revealing a rare and compelling coexistence of wilderness and urban life.

journeys.title: Royal Rajasthan Safari
journeys.description: Rajasthan unfolds as a land of layered histories, dramatic landscapes, and enduring regal traditions.
journeys.intro:
Rajasthan unfolds as a land of layered histories, dramatic landscapes, and enduring regal traditions. From arid plains and ancient forests to granite hills and walled cities, this region hosts a remarkable mosaic of habitats shaped by centuries of rule, culture, and resilience.

This immersive journey traces a refined arc through India’s most storied heartland,beginning with the architectural grandeur of Delhi and Agra, before venturing into the tiger-haunted ruins of Ranthambhore.

The experience then unfolds through the royal elegance of Jaipur and Udaipur, moves into leopard country amid Jawai’s striking granite formations, and concludes in the timeless splendour of Jodhpur, the Blue City of the Rajputs.
highlights: Discover Rajasthan’s royal and untamed spirit as you travel through historic cities, ancient forts, and vibrant wilderness landscapes. Enjoy expertly guided safaris in Ranthambhore and Jawai, stay in exquisite heritage hotels, and savour the region’s legendary cuisine. This journey seamlessly weaves together culture, wildlife, and refined luxury across some of India’s most iconic destinations.

body: Along the way, guests are immersed in India’s finest hospitality, soulful regional cuisine, and expertly guided safaris across some of the country’s most iconic wildlife landscapes,where history, wilderness, and royalty converge to leave a lasting impression.

Discover Rajasthan’s royal and untamed spirit as you travel through historic cities, ancient forts, and vibrant wilderness landscapes. Enjoy expertly guided safaris in Ranthambhore and Jawai, stay in exquisite heritage hotels, and savour the region’s legendary cuisine. This journey seamlessly weaves together culture, wildlife, and refined luxury across some of India’s most iconic destinations.

Arrive in India’s capital and explore its striking contrasts of Mughal monuments, colonial avenues, and vibrant marketplaces. Travel to Agra to witness the Taj Mahal in the golden light of dawn or dusk and visit the impressive Agra Fort. Evenings are spent in comfort at one of the region’s finest hotels.

Travel to Ranthambhore National Park, famed for its tigers roaming freely amidst ancient temples and crumbling Rajput fortifications. Enjoy guided safaris across lakes, grasslands, and rocky hillscapes. Between drives, relax at your lodge while immersing yourself in the rhythms of the forest.

Fly to Jaipur, the Pink City, where the Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and artisanal bazaars showcase Rajasthan’s royal artistry. Continue to Udaipur, the romantic city of lakes, where the shimmering Lake Pichola reflects palaces, temples, and ghats. Enjoy boat rides, heritage walks, and serene luxury.

Enter the dramatic landscapes of Jawai, where huge granite boulders conceal thriving leopard populations living alongside Rabari shepherds. Embark on leopard safaris, visit pastoral settlements, and experience the tranquillity of the Jawai Dam,often a haven for flamingos and migratory birds.

Conclude your journey in Jodhpur, the Blue City. Explore the majestic Mehrangarh Fort rising above a sea of indigo homes, marvel at the stepwells, stroll through the vibrant Sardar Market, and savor the city’s rich Marwari cuisine. Depart from Jodhpur with memories of Rajasthan’s royal soul.

Your Royal Rajasthan Safari opens in Delhi, a city forged by ambition and empire. From the rise and fall of Sultanates and Mughal dynasties to the quiet order of the British Raj, power has shaped this capital in stone and memory. Its monuments stand like chronicles of conquest and vision.
From here, you travel to Agra to stand before the Taj Mahal, born of love and loss, and walk the ramparts of Agra Fort, where emperors once ruled and destiny was decided.

The journey then turns toward Ranthambhore, where a 10th-century fort looms above forests, lakes, and abandoned temples. Once a royal hunting ground, this land has reclaimed its wild soul. Tigers move through ruins and shadows, and history yields to the primal rhythm of the forest.

From wilderness to royalty, you arrive in Jaipur, the meticulously planned capital of the Kachwaha Rajputs. Pink-hued streets, grand palaces, and celestial observatories reflect a civilisation guided by order, science, and artistry. Udaipur follows,romantic and resolute. Here, white palaces rise from still waters, carrying the legacy of the Mewar rulers who chose resistance over surrender.

journeys.title: The Southern Arc
journeys.bestMonths: February to May is the peak season, but talk to us about other possible seasons.
journeys.description: A verdant passage through South India’s forests, waterways and highlands, where exceptional richness is revealed one ecosystem at a time.
journeys.intro:
This journey enters a verdant realm of extraordinary richness, where South India’s forests and highland ecosystems form one of the subcontinent’s most important wildlife corridors. Within this globally recognised biodiversity hotspot, the landscapes chosen for this Journey change seamlessly between mist-covered hills, sprawling meadows, emerald forests and rivers winding through ancient woodland, creating a setting as remarkable as the wildlife it sustains.

The journey follows a graceful natural arc from the tranquil waters of Kapila, the river, anglicised as Kabini, to the storied forests of Bandipur, where some of India’s most compelling wildlife encounters can happen: tigers roam these forests, leopards appear along the woodland edge or equally famously – on trees, and large herds of elephants share the habitat with wild dogs and sloth bears.

Few places offer such an extraordinary concentration of wildlife, paired with the intimacy, beauty and sense of place that make these corners of southern India so distinctive.
highlights: This journey brings together two of South India’s finest wildlife ecosystems, where private boat- and land-safaris offer intimate access to extraordinary concentrations of wildlife. You are most likely to get to watch vast herds of elephants gathering along the waters, while tigers, leopards and the endangered wild dogs co-inhabit these wildernesses. Across the biodiverse Western Ghats, the experience extends to rare primates, reptiles and amphibians, including the lion-tailed macaque and the Nilgiri tahr, alongside a remarkable wealth of endemic species found nowhere else on Earth. With year-round access, accomplished naturalists and every detail thoughtfully taken care of, this all-inclusive Journey offers privileged time in the field, exceptional wildlife encounters and the rare pleasure of experiencing southern India at your preferred pace.

days.copy: Arrive in Bengaluru, the starting point of this Journey. Settle into your hotel before an introductory briefing with your naturalist, covering the landscapes ahead, wildlife behaviour, photography discussion and the logistics of the expedition.

days.label: Days 2-4
days.title: Kabini
days.copy: Travel by private road to Kabini, where tranquil backwaters, riverine forests and open grasslands create one of South India’s most rewarding wildlife landscapes. The region is renowned for its elephant gatherings, alongside opportunities to encounter tigers, leopards and wild dogs. Alternate between boat and jeep safaris, experiencing the wilderness from contrasting perspectives and gaining a deeper understanding of how wildlife lives in this water-rich habitat. Evenings are for quiet and leisure, and conversations with your naturalist on animal behaviour, tracking and the ecology of Kabini.

days.label: Days 5-7
days.title: Bandipur
days.copy: Continue to Bandipur National Park, an important part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, where dry deciduous forests, rolling hills and seasonal streams create a rich mosaic of habitats. Tigers, leopards, elephants and gaur inhabit these forests, alongside an impressive diversity of birdlife. Early morning safaris make the most of the gentle light and cooler hours, while afternoon drives offer the possibility of predators becoming active as the day begins to soften. Throughout, your naturalist brings context to tracks, calls and behaviour, transforming each safari into a more informed and rewarding experience.

days.label: Days 8-9
days.title: Coimbatore & Anamalais
days.copy: Travel onwards to Anamalai, a dramatic world of deep valleys, forested slopes and great endemism. Explore its evergreen forests in search of the elusive lion-tailed macaque, while discovering a remarkable diversity of reptiles, amphibians and birds found nowhere else. Here, altitude, rainfall and terrain combine to create one of the Western Ghats’ most distinctive ecosystems, offering a fascinating counterpoint to the forests encountered earlier in the journey.

days.label: Days 10-11
days.title: Eravikulam & Departure
days.copy: The final chapter takes you into the highlands of Eravikulam National Park, where expansive grasslands meet mist-covered mountains and ancient shola forests. Explore designated trails in search of the endemic Nilgiri tahr, with sweeping views extending across the surrounding peaks and tea estates. Montane birds, rare amphibians and specialised high-altitude flora add further depth to this remarkable biodiversity hotspot. Depart from Kochi with a Journey that has made you traverse the forests, waterways and mountain landscapes of South India, witnessing a memorable variety.

journeys.title: Terrific Terai
journeys.description: The Shivalik Range and the Terai together form a living threshold between mountain and plain, where the Himalaya slowly loosens into forested foothills, braided rivers,.
journeys.intro:
The Shivalik Range and the Terai together form a living threshold between mountain and plain, where the Himalaya slowly loosens into forested foothills, braided rivers, and fertile grasslands. Shaped by monsoon rhythms and ancient geology, this breathing landscape sustains an extraordinary richness of life.

The journey follows this wild corridor across four distinct reserves, each with its own character and pulse, from Corbett’s riverine forests, where tigers and elephants move through mist and water, to Rajaji’s sal woodlands resonant with birdsong and elusive leopards; from the quiet, little-trodden wilderness of Pilibhit to the wetland-laced expanses of Dudhwa.

Together, these landscapes unfold as a poetic passage of adventure and patience, offering intimate encounters with nature in all its shifting moods. Explore four iconic sanctuaries across the Terai and Shivalik foothills, each offering exceptional wildlife encounters with tigers, leopards, elephants, swamp deer, and rich birdlife.

Journey through a mosaic of forests, wetlands, and river systems, accessing lesser-visited wilderness areas that allow for more intimate and rewarding sightings. Accompanied by expert naturalists, and with the option of seamless travel via company-owned business jets, this all-inclusive itinerary delivers a deeply immersive and refined wildlife experience.

Arrive in India’s capital and settle in before your journey into the Terai begins. Your naturalist will conduct a brief orientation outlining upcoming landscapes, species, and logistics.

Travel to Jim Corbett National Park, India’s oldest tiger reserve. Its mix of riverine belts, dense sal forests, and wide grasslands offers ideal habitats for Bengal Tigers, Leopards, and Elephants. Morning and afternoon jeep safaris take you through varying terrain, increasing chances of sightings.
Corbett’s rivers support rich birdlife and crocodilians, while quiet forest trails reveal signs of movement from Jackals, Deer, and other mammals.

Continue to Rajaji National Park, where the foothills of the Himalayas meet sweeping grasslands. The park’s mosaic of riverine and sal forests supports Tigers, Leopards, and India’s largest Elephants herds. Open areas provide excellent photographic opportunities of ungulates such as Swamp Deer and Wild Boar. Birders enjoy sightings of hornbills, woodpeckers, and raptors patrolling the valleys.

Move into the quieter, less-visited wilderness of Philibit. Its forests and fields hold Leopards, Jungle Cats, Hyenas, and rich bird diversity. Safaris here focus on tracking signs, observing behavior, and exploring landscapes shaped by human-wildlife coexistence. The gentle pace allows for immersive nature photography and meaningful time in the field.

End your journey in the biodiverse expanses of Dudhwa National Park. Explore tall grasslands, wetlands, and dense sal forests on boat and jeep safaris. Look for endangered Swamp Deer, Marsh Crocodiles, and birdlife that thrives around its river systems. Trails occasionally reveal signs of Tigers and Leopards moving through the undergrowth. Evenings are reserved for debriefings, stargazing, or relaxed time in the lodge.

The journey through the Terai and Shivaliks unfolds as a gradual passage through some of India’s most dynamic ecosystems. Jim Corbett National Park sets the tone with dramatic river valleys and evocative dawn choruses, where tigers move silently through sal forests and elephants appear along riverbanks without warning.
In Rajaji National Park, the landscape opens into grasslands and wooded slopes, with the possibility of encountering leopards in their feral Shivalik habitat amid bird-rich sal forests.

The experience deepens at Pilibhit Tiger Reserve, where tall grasslands and quiet forest corridors offer a genuine chance of spotting a tiger moving through dense vegetation, an intimate and memorable sight unique to this landscape. The journey concludes at Dudhwa National Park, where wetlands and towering grasses reflect a world shaped by monsoon rhythms and seasonal migrations.
Together, these reserves reveal the larger story of the Terai: a vital wildlife corridor experienced with depth, comfort, and unhurried immersion.

journeys.title: Trail of the Himalayan Firefox
journeys.description: An intimate passage through Northeast India, from Singalila’s cloud forests and red pandas to Kaziranga’s rhinos and great floodplains.
journeys.intro:
This journey brings together two of Northeast India’s most extraordinary wildernesses – from the cloud forests and high ridgelines of the Himalaya to the vast floodplains of Assam. On the Singalila Ridge, rhododendron forests, swirling mists and dramatic mountain vistas create a fairytale-like setting for the elusive Red Panda, with views extending towards four of the world’s five highest peaks, including Mount Everest. It is a landscape of remarkable beauty and quiet discovery, where patience is richly rewarded.

From the highlands, you will descend into the lush floodplains of Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tall grasslands, wetlands and riverine habitats support thriving populations of Indian one-horned rhinos, elephants and an extraordinary diversity of birdlife. The contrast is markedly thrilling – from the quietude of Himalayan forests to expansive, wildlife-rich plains where the scale of the landscape grants every encounter to take on a different character.

A special visit to the Gibbon Sanctuary adds another rare dimension to this Journey, offering the opportunity to observe India’s only apes, the agile, arboreal hoolock gibbons, moving through the forest canopy. With accomplished naturalists who are our partners, seamless logistics and a direct contribution to red panda conservation, this carefully crafted Journey is the mingling of rare wildlife, extraordinary landscapes and meaningful conservation.

days.title: Delhi
days.copy: Arrive in India’s vibrant capital and settle into your hotel before the journey eastwards begins. Depending on your arrival time, explore Delhi’s celebrated old markets and historic quarters, or simply relax and ease into the expedition ahead.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Bagdogra & Siliguri
days.copy: Fly to Bagdogra and continue to Siliguri, the gateway to the Eastern Himalaya. Spend the evening at leisure, preparing for the ascent into the high-altitude forests of Singalila the following morning.

days.label: Days 3-6
days.title: Singalila Ridge
days.copy: Ascend to the spectacular Singalila Ridge, renowned for its panoramic views of the world’s highest peaks and exceptional opportunities to encounter the elusive red panda. Your lodge, situated across the border in Nepal, is reached through a formal immigration crossing, adding to the sense of remoteness and exclusivity. Each day begins at sunrise, with breakfast followed by dedicated bird photography and patient searches for red pandas alongside expert trackers. When a red panda is located, the group moves quietly into position, with porters assisting with photographic equipment and ensuring the experience remains comfortable and unobtrusive. Afternoons return to the forest and surrounding trails, offering further opportunities for Himalayan birdlife and occasional encounters with other mammals.

days.label: Day 7
days.title: Bagdogra to Guwahati
days.copy: Depart early from the lodge for Bagdogra Airport and board your afternoon flight to Guwahati. Settle into your hotel for the evening, with time to rest before continuing into Assam’s great wilderness.

days.label: Day 8
days.title: Kaziranga National Park
days.copy: Travel by private road to Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India’s most important strongholds for the Indian one-horned rhino. Arrive and settle into your wilderness lodge before beginning your exploration of this extraordinary floodplain landscape.

days.label: Days 9-11
days.title: Kaziranga Safaris & Gibbon Sanctuary
days.copy: Explore Kaziranga on morning and afternoon jeep safaris, moving through expansive grasslands, wetlands and woodland patches in search of elephants, wild water buffalo, tigers, rhinos and an exceptional diversity of birdlife. A dedicated visit to the Gibbon Sanctuary offers the rare opportunity to observe hoolock gibbons — India’s only apes — inhabiting the forest canopy. With expert naturalists accompanying each exploration, every outing brings greater insight into the ecology and wildlife of Assam.

days.label: Day 12
days.title: Departure to Delhi
days.copy: Return to Guwahati for your flight to Delhi, bringing this journey through the Eastern Himalaya and Assam to a close. For those wishing to continue, the journey can be extended into India’s renowned tiger country for a further chapter of wildlife exploration.

body: This journey brings together two of Northeast India’s most extraordinary wildernesses – from the cloud forests and high ridgelines of the Himalaya to the vast floodplains of Assam. On the Singalila Ridge, rhododendron forests, swirling mists and dramatic mountain vistas create a fairytale-like setting for the elusive Red Panda, with views extending towards four of the world’s five highest peaks, including Mount Everest. It is a landscape of remarkable beauty and quiet discovery, where patience is richly rewarded.

From the highlands, you will descend into the lush floodplains of Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tall grasslands, wetlands and riverine habitats support thriving populations of Indian one-horned rhinos, elephants and an extraordinary diversity of birdlife. The contrast is markedly thrilling – from the quietude of Himalayan forests to expansive, wildlife-rich plains where the scale of the landscape grants every encounter to take on a different character.

A special visit to the Gibbon Sanctuary adds another rare dimension to this Journey, offering the opportunity to observe India’s only apes, the agile, arboreal hoolock gibbons, moving through the forest canopy. With accomplished naturalists who are our partners, seamless logistics and a direct contribution to red panda conservation, this carefully crafted Journey is the mingling of rare wildlife, extraordinary landscapes and meaningful conservation.

faqs.question: Is this a fixed itinerary?
faqs.answer: No. This is something akin to a blueprint. Dates, pacing, lodge character, transfers and field priorities are refined around you and your preferences before confirmation.

faqs.question: Can the journey be shortened?
faqs.answer: Yes. The full route is designed as an immersive experience, but individual sections can be adapted depending on your priorities.

faqs.question: Can we add India’s cultural landmarks?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Any city/town in and around the regions/states part of this itinerary can be incorporated before, after or between the wildlife chapters.

faqs.question: Are the wildlife sightings guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. And we would never suggest otherwise. Wildlife is wild. Our job is to put you in the right landscape, at the right time, with the right people – and give the experience enough time to happen to you.

faqs.question: Is this suitable for families?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the journey is private, its pace can be adapted to different ages, interests and energy levels.

journeys.title: Uttarakhand Wildlife Circuit
journeys.description: There is a quiet poetry to this expedition, written in colour, contour, and the patient craft of nature across Uttarakhand’s most evocative terrains.
journeys.intro:
There is a quiet poetry to this expedition, written in colour, contour, and the patient craft of nature across Uttarakhand’s most evocative terrains. It reveals itself in sinuous rivers edged with pale stone, the austere grace of towering sal forests, and gentle transitions where grasslands open into wide, breathing valleys.

Light shifts constantly here, filtered through canopy, reflected off water, softened by mist, shaping landscapes that feel ancient yet alive. The journey begins in the storied forests of Jim Corbett National Park, where the Terai plains and Shivalik foothills converge in a mosaic of sal forests, riverine belts, and grasslands.

Tigers, leopards, elephants, and rich birdlife move through terrain long shaped by water and time. From here, the trail flows into the quiet magnificence of Rajaji National Park, a riverine wilderness where elephant herds traverse forest corridors and predators thrive in open, light-filled landscapes.
highlights: Explore Uttarakhand’s varied wilderness, from tiger-rich Terai forests to the serene Himalayan birding enclaves of Chopta, Sattal, and Pangot. Enjoy opportunities to photograph tigers, leopards, elephants, and an extraordinary array of Himalayan birds across contrasting landscapes. Seamlessly curated and all-inclusive, the journey blends jeep safaris, gentle treks, and guided nature walks led by expert naturalists, complemented by optional private jet travel for effortless comfort.
